QUOTE: "`mbedtls_memory_buffer_alloc_init(buf, len)` carves allocations out of a caller-supplied static buffer. It then calls `mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free()` to install its own calloc and free as the global pointers (`memory_buffer_alloc.c:566-576`)."
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer says the buffer allocator's init function calls the runtime setter to install its own calloc/free over the global pointers. It does not say outright that this is the only in-tree user, but it calls the allocator "the library's own allocator" and a consumer of the mechanism, and it names no other caller.
